documents: Domínguez-Cuesta et al. 2022, Understanding the retreat of the Jurassic Cantabrian coast (N. Spain): Comprehensive monitoring and 4D evolution model of the Tazones Lighthouse landslide, Marine Geology 106836, Journal Pre-proof PDF (35 pages)

entry.evidence: the mechanisms involved in regulating the style and pace of retreat remain poorly known

sequences.source_document: Domínguez-Cuesta et al. 2022, Journal Pre-proof PDF

steps.action: Report, citing the team's earlier conference abstract, that cracks linked to cliff retreat irreversibly damaged a restaurant more than 200 m inland near the Tazones Lighthouse.
steps.quote: a restaurant building located more than 200 m from the coastline was irreversibly damaged

steps.action: State four aims: characterize the instability type, quantify displacement from June 2018 to May 2020, establish conditioning factors, and relate acceleration to rainfall, soil moisture and wave height.
steps.quote: establish the relationships between landslide displacement acceleration and rainfall, soil moisture, and wave height

steps.action: Take the regional stratigraphy, the alterability of Lastres Fm. sandstone and the fault systems from published studies as the geological setting.
steps.quote: the Jurassic rocks of the region are affected by small-scale normal, reverse, thrust, and strike slip faults and open folds

steps.action: Note the published rival interpretation that local subsidence features are collapses of old jet-mining galleries.
steps.quote: Traditionally, local subsidence phenomena have been interpreted in this area as mining collapses

steps.action: Fly two UAV photogrammetric surveys (2018, 2019) with ground control points and process them in Agisoft Metashape into 3D point clouds, DSMs and 2.5 cm GSD orthophotos.
steps.quote: The photogrammetric processing was carried out with Agisoft Metashape software

steps.action: Check photogrammetric accuracy against GNSS-positioned checkpoints, reporting RMSE of 1.4 to 3.4 cm per axis.
steps.quote: error estimation was performed by means of checkpoints (12 in 2018, 7 in 2019) using GNSS positioning

steps.action: Design the monitoring network: 34 feno-type markers and 4 nails placed according to crack distribution, extended after new cracks appeared, surveyed by total station in 22 campaigns, with displacements under 2 cm treated as not significant.
steps.quote: The location of markers was selected after a field reconnaissance and according to the distribution of the ground cracks

steps.action: Compare four AEMET rain gauges against a new volunteer-run manual gauge 2.3 km from the site, and select the Luces-Aspo gauge for its complete series and good agreement.
steps.quote: had a complete series of monthly-accumulated precipitation values with a good correspondence with those recorded at the new manual station

steps.action: Take soil moisture as the Available Water Capacity index from AEMET daily water-balance models (kriged 25 km2 rasters), and take maximum daily Hs from the modelled SIMAR series.
steps.quote: Soil moisture content has been estimated by the analysis of the Available Water Capacity (AWC)

steps.action: Map the geomorphology at 1:15,000 and 1:1,500 from fieldwork, aerial, Google Earth and UAV imagery and a boat survey: the rasa, hanging valleys, a scour front, complex mass movements and open cracks, including old mortar-filled cracks seen in February 2018.
steps.quote: The new 1:15,000 scale cartography has enabled an in-depth description of the geomorphological features of the studied coastal segment

steps.action: Report cumulative marker displacements: 10 markers stable within uncertainty, 28 moving 0.06 to 15.08 m, with the largest movements in campaigns C7 and C15.
steps.quote: The remaining 28 markers display cumulative movements ranging between 0.06 m (FB1 and FB4) and 15.08 m (FG3)

steps.action: Identify, within the monitored period, the January-February and October-November 2019 rainfall and storm periods (daily peaks of 64.5 and 82.1 mm, Hs peaks, saturated soil) and quantify the share of total displacement in those intervals (Table 3).
steps.quote: For all markers, the largest shifts occurred in January and November 2019.

steps.action: Characterize bedrock discontinuities from field stations and drone point-cloud measurements (Compass plugin, Dips kinematic analysis), and measure a strength loss of more than 50% in weathered sandstone with a Schmidt hammer.
steps.quote: Three types of bedrock discontinuities have been identified: bedding S0: 002/14, and two joint families

steps.action: Describe the borehole cores (anthropogenic infill, very plastic clays with measured cohesion and strength), infiltration rates and water-table depths at eight water points.
steps.quote: the presence of levels of clays with very plastic behaviour is significant

steps.action: Classify the instability, after Varnes (1978), as a complex landslide whose crack evolution reflects a primary planar slide along S0 with secondary flows, topples and rock falls.
steps.quote: Crack evolution observed over the entire monitored period is closely related to a primary planar landslide following S0

steps.action: Compare ancient scars along the coast with the recent Tazones features, and read hanging valleys and cracks visible in the 2001 images as signs of episodic cliff retreat faster than fluvial incision.
steps.quote: ancient scars in the study area have similar dimensions and characteristics to recent ones observed in the Tazones Lighthouse area

steps.action: Compare displacement vectors, the vertical motion of FA3 and crack trends with the orientations of S0, J1 and J2 to support structural control of the slide.
steps.quote: pointing to a direction of movement consistent with the dip angle of bedding planes (S0: 002/14)

steps.action: Propose a mechanism: cement dissolution (cited) makes sandstone porous, saturation adds weight, and saturated marl beds act as slip planes, illustrated by the November 2019 FG3 slip.
steps.quote: marl beds probably work as slipping planes due to their plastic (ductile) behaviour once saturated

steps.action: Test the mining-collapse rival against field evidence: no mining galleries were found, but the rival is left undetermined rather than excluded.
steps.quote: we have not found unequivocal evidence of abandoned mining galleries within the study area

steps.action: Acknowledge that monthly marker data cannot separate wave forcing from rainfall and soil saturation as the trigger of accelerations.
steps.quote: it is not possible to discern whether point accelerations are more closely related to waves or to precipitation and soil saturation

steps.action: Analyse the 1960-2020 SIMAR Hs record and show that extreme wave events have become more frequent in the last decade and since 2018.
steps.quote: there have been 35 events with Hs ≥ 5.90 m, 54% of them concentrated in the last decade

steps.action: Cross-compare the climatic and wave series with displacement and report a positive, qualitative correlation: the largest displacements coincide with soil moisture above 90%.
steps.quote: shows a positive correlation, with increasing displacement when soil moisture content increases in response to rainfall episodes

steps.action: Check the relation on the January-May 2020 episode: a displacement pulse after the rainfall peak, then a decline as soil moisture fell below 90%.
steps.quote: The evolution of FC3, FD3, FG1, and FF1 markers in 2020 reveals the close relationship between sliding activation and soil moisture

steps.action: Defend the AWC soil-index proxy against its limitation (a soil of fixed thickness, whereas the mass is mostly bedrock) by arguing that weathering-enhanced bedrock porosity lets it track pore saturation.
steps.quote: The use of the AWC index to represent the evolution of soil moisture content has some limitations

steps.action: Set the result against other rocky coasts (Galicia, southern California) where rainfall, soil moisture and alternating marine action control cliff instability.
steps.quote: Precipitation and soil moisture content determine cliff instability as has been shown in other rocky coastal areas (Young et al., 2009)

steps.action: Keep the claim: a complex landslide with a primary planar slide, conditioned by lithology, structure and undercutting, triggered mainly by rainfall and soil moisture and coeval with storms; longer monitoring is called for to confirm it.
steps.quote: The main triggering factors controlling planar sliding are linked to variation in precipitation and soil moisture content

tree.answer: Active complex landslide with growing open cracks at the Tazones Lighthouse cliff
Displacement measured directly by total station; soil moisture inferred from a water-balance model
Characterize the instability type and its conditioning and triggering factors
Waves versus rainfall and soil saturation as triggers; mining collapse versus natural instability
Not separable: monthly data cannot discriminate waves from rain
Found: the 2019 storm and rainfall periods during live monitoring

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Nature repeated: two 2019 episodes plus a 2020 episode
Partly: the 2020 episode is consistent; no sensitivity tests
Kept as best explanation; waves only suggested; confirmation deferred

end.claim: The Tazones Lighthouse slope evolves as a complex mass movement with a primary planar slide along bedding S0, conditioned by lithology, structure and sea undercutting, whose largest accelerations (up to 15 m in total) coincided with periods of heavy rainfall, soil moisture above 90% and sea storms.

decisive_move.sentence: The 22-campaign total-station monitoring of 38 markers supplies the displacement time series without which neither the kinematics nor the link to rainfall and storms could be claimed.

gates.evidence: Markers were placed after the cracks appeared and according to their distribution. The rainfall, soil-moisture and wave series were assembled to address aim iv, but no hypothesis or threshold was stated beforehand (p. 6, 10). The correlation could in principle have failed (displacement not coinciding with storms), but it is assessed qualitatively on two episodes, waves and rain are not discriminated (p. 25), and confirmation is deferred to longer monitoring (p. 27).

imports.item: UAV structure-from-motion photogrammetry (Agisoft Metashape) producing point clouds, DSMs and orthophotos
CloudCompare Compass plugin for measuring structural planes in point clouds
Leica TC-407 total station and feno-type survey markers
NRCS-USDA Soil Taxonomy soil type and texture as water-balance model input
Corine Land Cover database for vegetation root depth

novelty_claims.quote: These events and signs have been detected by local people and researchers
constitutes a unique opportunity to understand the evolution of the Cantabrian Jurassic cliffs
has allowed a substantial advance in the understanding of the progress of the retreat of the Cantabrian Coast

limits:
No review file was supplied, although the acknowledgments name two anonymous referees and a review of an earlier version by A. Trenhaile (p. 3); a review sequence could not be coded.

The rainfall-displacement 'correlation' is a qualitative temporal coincidence over two main episodes (plus a 2020 pulse). No correlation coefficient or threshold is computed (inference from pp. 19-26).

The 2020 check (coded replication) comes from the same monitoring series and is post hoc.

Discontinuity orientations differ between sections: abstract and conclusions give S0 360/15-17, J1 262/85, J2 166/75; results give S0 002/14, J1 166/75, J2 085/89 (pp. 3, 21, 27). The text does not explain this.

Table 3 labels the first window January-February (C6-C7) while the text says February 2019 and also January (pp. 19-20). The Table 2 legend says December 2019 for markers installed in December 2018 (pp. 19, 21).

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Marker displacement magnitudes: estimate_with_resolution, with a 2 cm significance threshold (p. 11).
- Structural control by S0, J1 and J2: best_explanation (p. 24).
- Role of sea storms: suggested only, 'apparently related' (p. 3, 26).
- Mining-gallery rival: left undetermined, not excluded (p. 25).

Composition: trace_series was chosen because conditions are found and several independent data streams are combined into a best explanation. The core evidence, however, is live monitoring rather than traces of past events, so the fit is approximate.

The UAV-derived 'landscape deformation' analysis named in the abstract is not reported quantitatively in the results. The '4D model' is not presented as a formal model.

Marker placement and the timing of the analysis are not documented beyond the methods text. Whether any analysis choices were made after seeing the data cannot be judged (inference).

disagreements.target: Crespo et al. (2008), interpretation of local subsidence and lineal hollows as jet-mining gallery collapses
disagreements.support: Numerous field campaigns found no unequivocal evidence of mining galleries in the study area, though the authors leave the galleries' role undetermined.
disagreements.quote: no evidence of mining has been found during this research in the surroundings of the Tazones Lighthouse

disagreements.target: Defensive coastal investments on the Cantabrian Jurassic Coast (BOE, 2014; MITECO, 2021)
disagreements.support: The authors argue that such interventions ignore the retreat mechanisms that their monitoring aims to clarify; no direct evaluation of the interventions is given.
disagreements.quote: often disregarding the mechanisms and factors that modulate cliff retreat rate

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Three other AEMET gauges 10-19 km away; new discontinuous manual gauge 2.3 km away
alternatives_considered.reason: Complete monthly series with good correspondence to the new manual station

alternatives_considered.chosen: Both marine and continental factors retained as triggers; rainfall and soil moisture emphasized
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Waves as the trigger versus precipitation and soil saturation as the trigger
alternatives_considered.reason: Monthly marker data cannot discriminate; longer and daily monitoring needed
No unequivocal evidence of galleries found; role left undetermined

alternatives_considered.chosen: AWC soil-moisture index as proxy for saturation
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Water infiltration through crack systems feeding the rupture surface (named as a possible additional control)
alternatives_considered.reason: Weathering-increased porosity lets AWC approximate pore saturation of bedrock blocks
